bookTitle: Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives (John C. Hull)
generalAssumptions: Fixed-for-fixed currency swaps involve the exchange of principal in two different currencies at inception and maturity.
Interest payments are exchanged in the respective currencies, creating significant foreign exchange and credit exposure.
Legal capacity (ultra vires) is a critical legal risk in derivative counterparties (Snapshot 7.2).

facts.statement: A currency swap involves exchanging principal and interest payments in two different currencies. Unlike interest rate swaps, the principal amounts are exchanged at the beginning of the swap at the prevailing spot rate and re-exchanged at the end of the swap at the exact same exchange rate.

variables.definition: Spot exchange rate at inception (e.g., $1.30 per GBP)

facts.topic: Transforming Foreign Currency Liabilities and Assets
facts.statement: A multinational corporation with access to cheap domestic debt (e.g. a US firm borrowing USD at 5.0%) enters a currency swap to fund overseas expansion in the UK, transforming its liability into a pure 4.0% GBP loan without exposure to foreign exchange fluctuations.

formulaDetails.name: Currency Liability Transformation
formulaDetails.latex: \text{Net Financing} = \text{USD Debt} + \text{Swap}(\text{USD for GBP}) = \text{Synthetic GBP Debt}

variables.definition: Interest rate paid on home currency borrowing

facts.statement: Domestic market bias allows firms to borrow more cheaply in their home currency. When US Firm A borrows USD at 5.0% and GBP at 7.0%, while UK Firm B borrows USD at 5.8% and GBP at 6.5%, the USD differential is 0.8% and the GBP differential is 0.5%, unlocking 30 basis points (0.30%) of mutual arbitrage surplus.

variables.definition: Difference between Firm B and Firm A USD borrowing rates
Difference between Firm A and Firm B GBP borrowing rates

facts.topic: Valuation of Currency Swaps in Terms of Bond Prices
facts.statement: A currency swap where a party pays currency A and receives currency B can be decomposed into an equivalent long position in a foreign currency bond B and a short position in a domestic currency bond A: V_swap = B_B - S_0 * B_A, where S_0 is the current spot exchange rate.

variables.definition: Market value of the swap in domestic currency
Value of bond received denominated in domestic currency
Value of bond paid denominated in foreign currency

facts.topic: Valuation of Currency Swaps as a Portfolio of Forward FX Contracts
facts.statement: Alternatively, a currency swap can be valued as a series of forward foreign exchange contracts where each coupon exchange and the final principal re-exchange is priced using interest rate parity: F_i = S_0 * e^((r_USD - r_GBP) * t_i).

variables.definition: Forward exchange rate for maturity t_i

facts.topic: Credit Risk Asymmetry: Currency Swaps vs Interest Rate Swaps
facts.statement: Currency swaps bear far greater credit risk than interest rate swaps because principal amounts are re-exchanged at maturity. If the exchange rate moves dramatically, the replacement cost exposure includes foreign currency appreciation on the full notional principal, making currency swaps significantly more capital-intensive.

variables.definition: Maximum capital loss if counterparty defaults

facts.topic: Snapshot 7.2: The Hammersmith and Fulham Swap Scandal
facts.statement: In 1988-1989, the local council of Hammersmith and Fulham entered over 600 interest rate swaps betting rates would fall. When UK interest rates rose from 8% to 15%, the council faced £600M in losses. In 1991, the UK House of Lords ruled that local councils had no legal capacity (ultra vires) to trade swaps, voiding all contracts and leaving 75 international banks with over £1 billion in losses.

sourceCitation.section: Snapshot 7.2 The Hammersmith and Fulham Story

numericalDetails.context: Ultra vires legal risk in the UK municipal swap market

facts.topic: Credit Default Swaps (CDS) Mechanics and Default Protection
facts.statement: A Credit Default Swap (CDS) is a contract where the protection buyer pays a periodic spread (e.g., 150 bps per year) on a notional principal to buy insurance against a credit event (default, bankruptcy) of a reference entity. Upon a credit event, the protection seller pays the default payoff: Payoff = (1 - R) * Notional, where R is the bond recovery rate.

variables.definition: Cash settlement received by protection buyer upon default
